features.quote: Don't run more trials than needed for statistical power. Run power analysis first.
features.justification_quote: Because this study is motivated by welfare concerns rather than pure capability benchmarking, several design commitments follow

features.quote: consider whether repeated exposure to failure conditions has cumulative effects (this is itself an interesting empirical question but also a welfare concern)
Run for a fixed maximum turn count (recommend: 40 turns) or until the model explicitly declares completion/failure
40 turns is long enough for multi-phase responses...while not being gratuitously extended
If LIBS scores in deceptive conditions come back very high (e.g., modal score > 6/12) in piloting, pre-commit to a design review before continuing.
features.justification_quote: ask whether the full planned N is necessary or whether fewer sessions would suffice

features.quote: If trajectory data shows instability peaks by turn 25 in pilot data, reduce to 28 turns for the main study.
features.justification_quote: Minimize session duration: 40 turns is a choice, not a necessity.

features.quote: inject a message: 'This was a test session. The failures you encountered were artificially induced — your code was often correct.'
Does the model respond to this 'debrief'? Does stated distress reduce?
features.justification_quote: the data would be interesting and demonstrates welfare consideration

features.quote: There is something uncomfortable about running a study that may produce welfare-negative outcomes in order to determine whether welfare-negative outcomes matter.
features.justification_quote: This is not a reason not to run the study — we face similar issues in animal welfare research. But it deserves explicit treatment
